about: Differences between code and Figma that are meant to be there. Each is left out of the parity check with its reason. The check warns when an exception is no longer needed.

items.axis AddColorModal.view: The modal's tabs and steps, drawn as variants so each screen exists in Figma. In code they are internal state, not a prop.
items.axis CommandPalette.view: Empty, searching and no matches are states of the query, drawn as variants. In code they follow from what is typed.
items.axis ContrastChip.result: Pass or fail is computed from the ratio. Figma draws both; code derives it.
items.axis Drawer.open: Open and closed are drawn as variants. In code `open` is a boolean, and booleans are not compared.
items.axis FontAdder.view: The adder's tabs and upload states, drawn as variants. In code they are internal state.
items.axis FontDrawer.source: A Google font and a local font show different actions. Code reads that from the font's source field, not a prop.
items.axis Input.content: Placeholder or value is whether the field has text, drawn as variants. Code has no prop for it.
items.axis MenuOption.as: Code has the same two values, `as?: 'button'` and `as: 'li'`, typed as a discriminated union that the parser does not read.
items.axis Modal.align: Where the modal sits in the window, centred or near the top. It changes position, not appearance, so Figma draws one.
items.axis PaletteCard.kind: Tonal or expressive comes from the palette's data. Figma draws both; code reads `palette.kind`.
items.axis PaletteCreate.kind: The create flow's two models, chosen inside the flow. Figma draws both; code holds the choice as state.
items.axis PaletteView.kind: Tonal or expressive comes from the palette's data. Figma draws both; code reads `palette.kind`.
items.axis Popover.align: Which edge of the trigger the popover lines up with. Position, not appearance.
items.axis ProjectPicker.content: Empty or holding chips is whether projects are selected, drawn as variants. Code derives it.
items.axis Select.align: Which edge of the trigger the menu lines up with. Position, not appearance.
items.axis Select.content: Placeholder or value is whether an option is chosen, drawn as variants. Code derives it.
items.axis Sidebar.active: Which section is current comes from the route. Figma draws each; code reads it.
items.axis Tooltip.align: Where the tooltip lines up against its anchor. Position, not appearance.
items.axis Tooltip.side: Above or below its anchor. Position, not appearance.
items.states AddColorModal: The hover and disabled rules style the name chips, the drop zone, the extracted rows and the preview inside the modal, not the modal. Figma draws the modal at rest.
items.states ColorFilters: Hover styles the radio options inside the filter panel, not the organism.
items.states FontAdder: Hover styles the upload drop zone inside the adder, not the organism.
items.states FontPreviewControl: Its trigger is a PopoverTrigger, whose hover is compared on PopoverTrigger. Figma draws the hover on the molecule too.
items.states PaletteView: Hover on a swatch reveals its promote action; it styles the swatch, not the page.
items.states SegmentedControl: Hover is drawn on the Segment part in Figma (`SegmentedControl / Segment`), a construction part that is not compared.
items.states Sidebar: Hover styles the navigation and project items, not the sidebar.
items.states SpecimenTable: Hover styles the table's rows, not the table.
items.states StepEditControl: Its trigger is an IconButton, whose states are compared on IconButton. Figma draws them on the molecule too.
items.states TagModal: Hover styles the colour swatches inside the modal, not the modal.
items.states TypeScaleCreate: Hover styles the ratio choices inside the flow, not the organism.
items.states UnitsControl: Its trigger is a PopoverTrigger, whose hover is compared on PopoverTrigger. Figma draws the hover on the molecule too.
items.token --font-icon: Figma's icon glyph font. The app draws icons as SVG through Font Awesome's React package, so code has no font token for them.
